correctness.rationale: For a permutation to be a square, each even cycle length must occur an even number of times; odd lengths are unrestricted. The labelled EGF is A(z)H(z) with A(z)=sqrt((1+z)/(1-z)) and H(z)=product_even cosh(z^j/j). The coefficient asymptotic A_n~sqrt(2/pi)n^-1/2 and the even-factor fractional moment for alpha>1/2 justify the coefficient ratio and independent short-cycle limits; no finite test extrapolation. Bounded-degree effective Hanf locality reduces every first-order sentence to finitely many thresholded short-cycle counts, since the long-path local type occurs arbitrarily often with high probability. Disjoint directed cycles are definable, yielding the reverse inclusion. For finitely many j the event algebra lies in Q(e^(1/D)); odd Poisson presence indicators have atom sizes tending to 0, proving density. The proof restricts to the successor binary-relation language, fixed sentences, and uniform conditional law, not the distribution of the square of a uniformly random permutation.
